1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to the Certified ScrumMaster Exam Prep Masterclass. This is Module 0, the course introduction. In the next few minutes you will see who the course is for and what you will be able to do. You will see how the exam works, what the course is built on, and how each module is organized. Then you will learn how to get the most from it. The idea is simple: learn Scrum, and then learn how the exam asks about it.

1.title: Who This Course Is For
1.text: This course is for you if you are preparing for the CSM exam, with or without a class behind you. If Scrum is new, each idea is taught briefly from zero. If you already attended a class, you get a fast revision of what the exam asks. Either way, about half of the course goes to how the exam asks: the traps, the practice questions and the technique. And in every module you will meet a team, and act as its Scrum Master.

1.title: What You Will Be Able to Do
1.text: By the end of the course you will be able to do five things. Explain Scrum in the Guide's own terms: its theory, its pillars and its values. Describe the accountabilities, the events and the artifacts, and how they connect. Handle Scrum Master situations such as facilitating, coaching, impediments and the organization. Spot the common traps before they spot you. And manage the clock on a fifty-question exam. The aim is applying Scrum, not only remembering it.

1.title: The Exam in Numbers
1.text: The exam in numbers. Fifty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes. You need thirty-seven correct, which is seventy-four percent. The questions come from the learning objectives and the Scrum Guide. The exam is taken online after the course, and it is not proctored. It is open book: you may use the Scrum Guide and your course materials. Always confirm the current format, fees and eligibility on Scrum Alliance's site before you book. Module eighteen covers exam technique.

1.title: What the Questions Look Like
1.text: What do the questions look like? Think of two kinds. A situational question tells a short story about a team, and asks what the Scrum Master should do, or which statement is true. A recall question asks a fact: who, when, how long, or how many. Both are answered from the Guide, and the course practices both. Every topic module has three situational questions and two recall questions. For a situational question, return to the Guide's rules and the Scrum Master's accountabilities.

1.title: The Official Basis
1.text: What is the course built on? The Scrum Guide comes first, and it always wins. Next come the Agile Manifesto and the five Scrum values. Then the fifty-two official learning objectives: twenty-four for Scrum Foundations and twenty-eight for the CSM. For the objectives the Guide does not answer, such as facilitation, technical debt or the organization, the course uses public Scrum Alliance and practitioner guidance. If any source disagrees with the Guide, the Guide wins.

1.title: What Is In, and What Is Out
1.text: What is in, and what is out? In: everything in the Guide, the Manifesto and how Scrum reflects it, the five values, and all fifty-two learning objectives. Out: story points and user stories as required methods, velocity as a method, Kanban and scaling frameworks, and certification fees and renewal. Module eighteen explains why Scrum Alliance treats story points as absent from the Guide.

1.title: How the Course Is Built
1.text: The course has nineteen modules. Modules one and two lay the foundations. Modules three to five cover the Scrum Team. Modules six to nine cover the Sprint and its events. Modules ten to twelve cover the artifacts and their commitments. Modules thirteen and fourteen cover Scrum Master skills. And modules fifteen to eighteen are for practice: a scenario workshop, a traps clinic, a quick-reference recap, and the exam technique with a final check.

1.title: Labels You Will See
1.text: You will see three labels. Exam Tip marks a rule of thumb for answering. Beyond the Guide marks content that a learning objective asks for but the Guide does not state, such as practical steps, lists and examples. It comes from public Scrum sources, so treat it as exam practice, not as Guide text. And Old wording marks a term from the earlier edition of the Guide that a question may still use. It appears only where it is a trap.

1.title: How Each Module Works
1.text: Every topic module has the same shape. It starts with what you will learn, and a short case check-in. Then come the concepts, with diagrams. Then the traps: what the exam expects. Then a recap, and five practice questions with an answers slide. When a question appears, pause, and choose your answer before the answer is given. That habit is worth more than any other single thing in this course.

1.title: Meet the Running Case: RideLoop
1.text: Meet the running case. RideLoop is the app and station software of a city bike-share, run by Lakeshore Transit. The Product Goal: riders unlock a bike and pay in under twenty seconds at ninety-five percent of stations. You are the Scrum Master. Maya Okafor is the Product Owner, and there are seven Developers. Around them are Grace Whitfield, the Director of Operations, the Platform Team, the Station Crew, and Customer Support. The case is fictional.

1.title: How to Use the Course
1.text: How to use the course. Read the Scrum Guide once before Module one, which takes about twenty minutes, and again at the end. Take the modules in order. Answer each question before the answer is shown, and redo the ones you missed. Use Module fifteen to practice the method, and Module sixteen to spot traps. In the last two days, use Module seventeen every day, and Module eighteen for the final check.

1.title: Next Steps
1.text: Next steps. First, read the Scrum Guide once; it takes about twenty minutes. Then start Module one: the definition, the theory and the pillars. Keep going in order, and answer every question before the answer. Confirm the exam details on Scrum Alliance's site. And remember: from the next module on, you are the Scrum Master of RideLoop. Welcome to the team.
